messages:
Esi (Customer): Hey team — started seeing flaky SSE responses this morning. Client receives a few chunks then connection dies. Browser console shows "net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET" and our Node backend shows `write EPIPE` in logs. Happens more when traffic spikes.

Esi (Customer): Repro steps: 1) open SSE /v1/stream with prompt that generates ~2k tokens, 2) throttle client reading to 50ms pauses between reads (we simulate slow consumer), 3) after ~20s stream stops with socket write error on server.

Esi (Customer): Example client we use (node):
```js
const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'GET' });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true) { const {done, value} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; await sleep(50); // simulate slow consumer
  // process chunk
}
```

Leah (Support): thanks for the clear repro. Can you paste the server-side stack for the EPIPE? Also which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

Esi (Customer): Hosted. Server logs: `Error: write EPIPE at afterWrite (net.js:...) at Socket._writeGeneric (internal/streams/writable.js:...)` plus a handful of `stream aborted` messages from the runtime.

Leah (Support): pinging runtime team — Priya / Omar. Does this look like classic slow-consumer backpressure causing the runtime to abort?

Priya (Runtime): looks likely. Quick questions: 1) Are you using streaming with large chunk sizes or flushing full model token batches in single write? 2) Any client-side proxies (nginx) between browser and our API?

Esi (Customer): We stream token batches of ~512 bytes per write. No external proxy, direct to Redwood hosted endpoint.

Omar (SRE): this matches a pattern we saw once: if the consumer stalls, the OS socket send buffer fills and writes eventually return EPIPE/EAGAIN. Runtime currently tries to flush large writes atomically which can blow through the buffer if consumer doesn't drain. The server then takes the path of aborting the connection to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Omar (SRE): Quick triage I ran: reproduced locally by adding an artificial delay in the client read (your 50ms). Server-side tcpdump shows payload queues building then RST from server process after repeated EAGAIN.

Priya (Runtime): suggested short-term mitigation — reduce per-write payloads and add exponential backoff on EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK instead of abort. Also enable chunked writes (e.g., 64-128 byte pieces) and make write path non-blocking with bounded in-memory queue.

Leah (Support): For the customer workaround: 1) adjust client to read continuously (avoid artificial pauses), 2) if using Node clients, increase stream consumer throughput (reduce sleep), or set higher highWaterMark on the reader, 3) temporarily reduce model output rate/sequence length where possible.

Esi (Customer): We can try reducing client-side pauses but we can't guarantee consumer won't be slow in production (some mobile clients pause while in background). Would prefer a server-side fix.

Priya (Runtime): Understood. Action items: A) Add write-chunking: split tokens into smaller writes (config flag: streaming.chunk_size_bytes), B) Change write error handling: on EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK, enqueue write and retry using event-loop backoff rather than immediate abort, C) Add per-connection ring buffer with hard cap and a close path that returns a clear SSE event before tear-down so clients can reconnect gracefully.

Priya (Runtime): I'll open a PR with the minimal patch: chunking + non-abort retry. ETA for canary release: 48 hours. We'll include a feature flag so we can toggle if any regressions.

Omar (SRE): Also adding observability: emit metric `sse.slow_consumer.count` and sample socket send-queue depth. That will help correlate customer reports with kernel queue saturation.

Leah (Support): Next steps for us: 1) enable flag on a small canary pool, 2) ask Esi to test canary URL, 3) if passed, roll to broader pool.

Esi (Customer): Happy to test. Can you give a canary endpoint and instructions? Also would like the server to send a final SSE event like `event: aborted
data: reason=slow_consumer` before closing if possible — makes reconnection easier.

Priya (Runtime): we'll add an attempt to emit `event: aborted` with reason when we decide to close due to backpressure. If socket already broken we can't. We'll try to send it and then close gracefully. Canary URL: https://canary.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream?customer=esi-abc

Leah (Support): Esi — please test against that URL using your slowed reader and paste logs.

Esi (Customer): Testing now. Reproduced earlier failure in <1min on prod but canary looks promising so far — I see continuous small chunks and no EPIPE after 10m of slowed reading. Confirming reconnection behavior: server sent `event: aborted
data: reason=slow_consumer` once when it did hit the cap, then allowed reconnect.

Leah (Support): Awesome. Priya/Omar — recommend scheduling the rollout after 24h canary and metric review. Also add a small blurb to the docs about recommended client behaviour (drain promptly, use auto-reconnect) and the new server-side flag.

Priya (Runtime): will do. I'll follow up with the PR link and the flag name.

Esi (Customer): Thanks everyone — this is a workable path. We'll keep monitoring and reach out if we see regressions. :thumbsup:
